name: Snow removal

pf.license.need: No statewide snow-removal license is known so far. Where a state's or city's rules require a license or a business registration, the form asks for it.
pf.license.ask: The company's business registration, or a city business license where the city asks for one.
pf.license.who_holds: The business. Plow drivers and shovelers need no license of their own unless the state's form says so. A driver's license fits the truck they drive.
pf.license.check: none: Rosie never looks up, checks or confirms a license, insurance or registration (D96); anything shown is as given by the business, not checked by Rosie
pf.license.blocks_live: nothing waits on a license (D96): the business and each person go live once set up and the owner says yes; a job the owner says needs a license they don't have isn't booked
pf.license.insurance_bond: General liability and commercial auto insurance are asked for. They are shown as given by the business, not checked by Rosie.
pf.license.background_checks: Only where the state's rules require them, or as the business's own word.
pf.license.not_this_work: Roof snow and ice dams are roofing work, licensed in some states. Hauling snow away by truck isn't offered here.

pf.services.pattern: Set service on a route: homes and businesses join a route, and the crew comes when the snow passes the trigger, in route order, with no set time.
pf.services.trigger: 2 inches at the business's own check point, any hour. One push per storm; a second push only when a storm passes 12 inches. The owner calls each storm with one text.

words: someone trapped, hurt or stuck in the cold
a fallen power line in the snow
a car stuck with someone inside, or its tailpipe buried

what_happens: Someone trapped, hurt or without heat in the cold: call 911 now. A snow crew can't answer an emergency. No booking.
A fallen power line: stay far away from it, and call 911 and the power company. No booking until it's safe.
A car stuck with someone inside: clear the tailpipe or open a window, and call 911 if anyone feels sick.
Roof snow or ice dams: that's roofing work, so the AI can look for a roofer. Stay out from under the roof edge where ice hangs. The driveway and walk can still be booked.
Ice hanging over a walk or door: use another door until it's down. The crew skips that part of the walk and tells the customer in writing.
pf.safety.booking_goes_on: Yes, for roof snow or hanging ice: the driveway and walk can still be booked. No, for anyone in danger, no heat or a power line.

pf.visit.check_in: Nobody needs to be home: no check-in code. The route lead texts OMW about 10 minutes out, then DONE with a photo. At the yard: the code at the counter.
pf.visit.storm_call: The owner, or a route lead the owner names, texts STORM ON with the depth. Rosie then texts each stop its arrival window from route order, plan stops first. Each DONE keeps the later windows right. No call, or under the trigger: no push and no charge, and each stop is told.
pf.visit.how_it_is_done: Plowed between the stakes. The front walk and steps shoveled. Ice melt where asked, pet-safe on request. Snow piled where the customer chose, never into the street, onto a sidewalk or onto a neighbor's land.
pf.visit.cars: A car left in the driveway: cleared around at full price, with a photo, as the customer agreed when booking.
pf.visit.changes_at_visit: Extra walks or a buried mailbox only when the customer says yes by text, priced first.
pf.visit.proof_done: DONE with a photo of the cleared driveway and walk, from the street.
pf.visit.price_at_visit: None: every push is priced before, from the list or from photos.
pf.visit.breakage: A clipped sprinkler head, a lawn torn up or a curb scraped: photos the same day, the facts to the customer and the owner; the owner decides how to make it right. Rosie never admits fault or offers money.
pf.visit.berm: A city plow berm across the driveway's end: cleared free, once per storm, within 12 hours of the push.

pf.money.start: Per-push plans and one-time pushes: a card saved at booking, charged at each DONE, or nothing taken and the bill texted after each push. Seasonal contracts and lane seasons: paid in full when booking (a lane season once both sign), or a season in 3 payments. At the yard: nothing taken; paid at the counter, including trailer fills priced from photos and salt by weight priced at the scale.
pf.money.light_winter: Per-push plan: no snow over the trigger, no push, no charge. Seasonal contract: one price, not refunded in a light winter.
pf.money.deposits: None by default. A seasonal contract can be paid in full when booking, within the state's caps. Deposit cap: from the state form.
pf.money.fees: The trip charge ($30 in the example): only when the crew comes and can't plow, or for a skip sent after the routes started, and only if the owner confirms it. No answer, no fee. Never more than one push. At the yard, a $20 fee only on a load paid ahead and missed.
pf.money.ending: One reply ends a plan any time. Pushes already done stay paid. Seasonal payments already due aren't refunded.
pf.money.emergency_prices: Where the state's rules limit price rises in a declared emergency, prices stay inside that limit.
pf.money.plans: Each push is charged at its own DONE. Rosfield's $2 counts once a month for a plan.
pf.money.tips: A tip line only if the owner turns it on; all to the crew.
pf.money.tax: A sales tax line only where the state taxes snow removal or salt, from the state form.

pf.rules.city_rules: Where a city sets a deadline to clear sidewalks after snow, the front walk is cleared inside it, and the plan's terms say so. Where a city bans pushing snow into the street, the crew never does.
pf.rules.emergency: A price limit in a declared emergency, where the state's rules set one.
pf.rules.written_contract: Above an amount, where the state's rules require it (business lots, seasonal contracts).

Flow B is the usual side: Lee Snow & Lawn (snow removal, plus lawn mowing as its second kind of work). Flow A is the less usual side: Lee Salt Supply, Sam's second company, a salt yard where a customer books a load-out time and Shay loads the truck.

Names: Jordan and Casey become route leads Rory and Devon; Riley and Avery become yard hands Shay and Remy; the master's partner Jamie becomes Lou. Addresses: 62 Ridge Rd (Alex), 400 Mill Rd (Lee Snow & Lawn), 90 Depot St (the yard).
